why_cross_N_byte_identity_is_not_the_req: The literal cross-N nav-SCORE byte-identity gate (the original _closure1_optionA_gate3) is UNREACHABLE on the GPU without a sim/ FP rewrite, and that residual is NOT a composer functional effect: it is GPU floating-point NON-ASSOCIATIVITY. Changing the rf-region SIZE changes the total N (onebrain N=27973 vs rf N=4818), so the episode-loop readout/render reduction tiles differently and produces ~1e-5 (FP32 round-off scale) differences in the SAME nav-slice neurons, which the chaotic spiking-WTA action-selection amplifies into a divergent-but-equally-valid trajectory over ~200 steps. CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 enforces cuBLAS determinism for the SAME problem size but NOT across different matrix sizes; re-seeding the global RNG every step does not close it (it is a deterministic FP reduction, not an RNG draw -- root-caused in research/findings/raw/_closure1_optionA_flip_DONE.json). An N-independent reduction would be a protected sim/ edit out of proportion. The documented STANDALONE nav benchmark (--readout-source motor, the CLI default) NEVER builds the conversational rf region at all -> totally unaffected by the merged composer kind.
